title: Creating Targeted, Interpretable Topic Models with LLM-Generated Text Augmentation
venue: 10th International Conference on Computational Social Science (IC2S2 2024), extended abstract; arXiv 2504.17445
subcategory: LLM text augmentation before topic modelling
task: Targeted, research-question-driven topic modelling of short texts
problem: Topic models produce general themes and need subjective interpretation; seeded models place a burden of prior knowledge on researchers.
architecture: GPT-4 writes a short description of the primary actor in each headline (prompt encodes the research goal without naming expected actors); BERTopic is run on these descriptions instead of the raw headlines; baseline BERTopic on raw headlines.

datasets.name: GDELT
datasets.details: 11,704 online news headlines about critical race theory

key_results: Augmented model groups headlines by actor type (governors, legislators, teachers, parents), whereas the baseline mixes school boards, a supreme court justice, parents and teachers in its largest topic.
strengths: Simple way to steer unsupervised topics toward a research question without topic-specific seeds.

limitations.text: Quality of GPT-4 descriptions checked only on a sample; performance may vary across applications.
No quantitative metric, single case study, two-page extended abstract.
